title:
CLO 2026 Academic Month  
Weaving dreams from scratch, garment assembly by sequence, CLO lets creativity grow freely
description: CLO 2026 Official Academic Monthly Course Review Now Available! Lecturer Huang Manhang from China Academy of Art provides an online explanation of the process and experience of creating a portfolio using CLO.
transcript:
Hello everyone, I am Huang Maihang from the Chinese Academy of Fine Arts.  
I am currently a senior fashion designer.  
I am very happy to be able to join this live broadcast.  
Thank you for the invitation.  
Let me introduce myself first.  
I graduated from Guangzhou Academy of Fine Arts.  
I am now studying fashion design at the Chinese Academy of Fine Arts.  
Besides fashion design, I also like to broaden my interests.  
I am very interested in photography and makeup, which are related to fashion.  
At the same time, they also greatly inspire my design work.  
Let me share some of my personal works.  
These are some of my previous makeup works.  
You can see that I like to use very vivid colors,  
for example, silver and light colors.  
I like to use contrasting colors to express a sense of conflict.  
I rarely use black and white in my designs.  
On the left is a work I previously created.  
On the right is another of my previous works.  
They all share the same style as my makeup.  
I would like to show you some of my previous works.  
My earlier design works are strongly connected to the projects I am about to introduce.  
My design style has always been like this.  
It has had a huge impact on my 3D work.  
I want to show you some works I made during my studies at the Chinese Academy of Fine Arts.  
This is the first one.  
There are two parts to this student course:  
the first is individual projects, and the second is group projects.  
This is the first Collex 93 3D wear I used.  
I combined Collex 94 and Collex 90+.  
This is another combination of Collex 94 and Collex 95%.  
But this class lasts a total of seven weeks, about two months. I can’t just do a little.  
Then I can show you a more explosive video made by me and my team members.  
I’m not sure what to do.  
I’m going to show you everything.  
Thank you for watching.  

Okay, after watching the video, I believe everyone is still shocked by the colors because I basically used all the colors I could, and I hardly used any black or white, except for the teeth, which are white.  
So you can see there are some tooth elements in it. This also inspired the project I will talk about later.  

Now let me introduce how this course is structured in school.  
The course lasts about seven weeks, a total of 49 days.  
It is divided into individual and group work.  
Individuals can find their own design style early on and quickly learn basic skills.  
The group work helps students build better connections and learn cooperation skills.  

Apart from Clo3D, there are also applications of AIGC and multi-application mixed workflows, including Nomad, Blender, TouchDesigner, and others.  
The skills covered in this short seven-week period are very broad.  

In other words, as a fashion designer,  
my favorite photography and makeup have all transformed from traditional to virtual forms.  
This is a very connected and innovative approach.  
It’s a big step forward for me and a brand new experience.  

Next, I want to talk about the inspiration and theme source for this project.  
Many people fear pain, including myself, because I experienced a long period of loneliness. Although it is over now, that long loneliness had a big impact on my life,  
accompanied by pain and discomfort, which required gradual adaptation and acceptance.  

When I share this kind of pain, I don’t want it to feel too painful.  
Because you might think you only do things every day when happy, so if you want happiness, why not express it in a happier way?  
So I basically used a lot of happy colors, such as many contrasting colors like red and green, or yellow and purple.  

Though the way of expression is unpleasant, having many colors can also make people feel numb or slightly uncomfortable.  
That is the kind of visual style I want to explore.  

I looked at some styles I mentioned above:  
The first is Pe, a famous Asian cultural style favored by Latino alcoholics,  
which expresses its existence through teeth.  

Then there is Acid Wave.  
The most striking feature of this style is the use of many bright, bumpy colors mixed together,  
creating a kind of acidic feeling that looks visually chaotic and sour.  
It is also a music style.  

The last is Eye Spy.  
I believe everyone, including my generation, has seen “Visual Discovery.”  
In fact, Eye Spy is the original version of Visual Discovery.  
It contains many small scenes, very delicate and rich, with a little poem below to help you find treasures in the scene.  
I hope the videos and scenes I create can also have such delicacy and discovery.  
So I consider this a very important reference.  

In the previous video, you also saw four characters:  
Door Tooth, Tiger Tooth, Old Tooth, and Sting Tooth.  

The first red character is Tiger Tooth, also called Full Tooth.  
Why? Because Tiger Teeth are the ones we most need to show off and fiercely defend in our mouths.  
They are the sharpest and most pointed.  
So the image and design I gave it are sharp, pungent, and avant-garde.  

The second is Door Tooth.  
Why does Door Tooth wear a suit?  
Because Door Tooth is the first tooth visible at the front of the mouth, like the front door.  
If the front door is crooked, people will notice immediately.  
So I wanted to give it a more formal feeling, hence the suit.  
Though it isn’t a full suit, I wanted it to feel complete.  
The top hat is also a variation of the outfit, making it more tooth-like and fun.  

The third is Old Tooth.  
Old Tooth is a large tooth in the middle of the mouth responsible for biting.  
It is very big.  
I drew many elements and inspirations from Old Tooth’s image for my clothing,  
and I added bite marks to the clothes to simulate this state.  

The fourth is Sting Tooth.  
Why is it a child?  
Because the second tooth emerges during maturity, so its age is the youngest among all types.  
We set it to be a smart, lively, and cute child.  
This creates a unique feeling.  

From my introduction, you can guess each tooth has a different personality.  
What we want to do is adapt the characters’ personalities to their teeth,  
adding traits people might encounter in real life.  

Now, the most important part is the application and implementation of technology.  
I think the best experience with Clo3D is that it is a very efficient tool.  
Of course, this is obvious.  
Look at the picture on my right — it shows some process of pattern making and materials.  
In Clo3D, you can greatly reduce your learning curve.  
You can try things quickly without worrying if they will work.  
Because you need to try first, then make it work slowly.  
So I think this is a very good tool.  

As the teacher said, they often use this to sketch during project development.  
I think it is very free and flexible.  

For example, the image on my right is a round set of tiger teeth.  
I imported it into Blender for re-coloring, but it is still Clo3D.  
In fact, normal cloth is very difficult to achieve this kind of shine and exquisite feel.  
You can try very rich material combinations and dynamic displays —  
like the video of a personal project I showed earlier.  

You can also try crafts you have never attempted in real life.  
I think that is great.  

Of course, mastering this technology is very important.  
It is also a very useful skill for students.  
Many industries now, not only clothing design but also the gaming industry,  
have already started requiring game clothing designs and related 3D software skills.  

So Clo3D is very good and important for the future.  
Not only Clo3D but also Blender, Nomad, and other 3D tools are important.  
They facilitate communication.  

For instance, if you communicate with a tablet, it’s hard to add or subtract details here and there.  
It’s difficult to achieve everything at once.  
But you can use Clo3D quickly, which is like using the same “grammar” to say the same thing.  

During the process, there are many challenges.  
One is, since I started from zero,  
moving from real materials to virtual ones is difficult.  
Sometimes I don’t know which real-life action corresponds to a function.  
So sometimes I feel uncertain about how to use certain features.  
But this is normal.  

There is also the issue of easy piercing and tearing.  
For example, my tablet is very wide, and I want to inflate it inside.  
In real life, we can either inflate or stuff it.  
The concept of parameter simulation in the computer is to balance pressure on both sides.  
Otherwise, the cloth will either collapse or float away.  
Because my clothes were inflated, they often floated away.  
This requires more practice to avoid mistakes.  

There is also gravity and physical properties.  
This relates to fabric behavior.  
If a fabric is unsuitable for a property, you need to try different fabrics to improve the effect.  

On the right is a design of a simple leg cover.  
In real life, it needs an elastic band to tie it up.  
So it also requires a similar component in Clo3D.  

After using Clo3D, I found the connection between 2D and 3D in real life is stronger.  
I understand what something should look like flat,  
but also how it looks three-dimensionally on the human body.  

However, there is a difficulty.  
It’s easy to sew incorrectly.  
The sewing concept in real life and in Clo3D is the same,  
but in 3D it’s easy to make mistakes or be unfamiliar with technical operations, leading to errors.  
This was a frequent mistake I made at the beginning.  

The third important point is that it’s not just Clo3D anymore.  
You can see this screenshot of me.  
At the top, there are Blender, GLTF, MTL, FBX, and other formats.  
The third is called “pattern,” various patterns.  

My workflow is:  
build clothes in Clo3D,  
go to Nomad to adjust the model and accessories,  
then go to Blender for rendering.  
After rendering, the scene is finalized in Blender,  
then sent to AI for video generation.  

So there are many steps.  
You need to know which software is compatible with which file format.  
You must remember clearly, otherwise data loss can happen.  

For example, I once transferred from Nomad to Blender or vice versa and forgot steps.  
It’s easy to lose data or have materials damaged in Clo3D.  
Look at the person on my right — after import, the material deformed.  
I had to go back to Clo3D to redo it, wasting time.  

Another point is the AI generation part.  
You can see these four squares — these are what I used to create the face of the person on the right.  
I needed a very long description to get a picture that was about 70% accurate.  
So AI still needs time to train.  

I recommend Nanobanana.  
I think Nanobanana is the smartest AI because it follows your instructions cleverly.  
MidJourney has its own ideas and adds elements on its own.  
AI requires you to spend time training it,  
and you need to have a certain aesthetic and design thinking.  

Finally, each software has a different workflow.  
You need to be clear about what each software does to avoid confusion.  

This is also related to teamwork in projects.  
Some of us worked on clothing and makeup,  
some on video production,  
and some on scene creation.  

Here is a picture of me creating configurations and adjusting models in Nomad.  
Nomad works well combined with Clo3D.  
Nomad lets you sculpt directly with your hands, like molding clay.  
It’s more intuitive.  
For harder materials, I use Nomad to combine them.  
It also supports some pre-rendering.  

For example, the colorful image on my left is a lighting render.  
I think it looks very cool.  
Then I went to Blender to render this.  
I adjusted the face in Nomad, but the model source is from Clo3D.  

This is a picture of me.  
Because I created it with Clo3D, I need to do post-processing to inspire video or stronger visual effects.  
On the left is a GLB file, which can be opened directly on Apple computers.  
It has a kind of 7P effect.  
I think it looks good.  

On the right is me before making the video,  
using some pictures for post-processing.  

This is another workflow for makeup.  
Makeup is first created and rendered in Blender.  
You can see this rendering.  
This one is rendered in Blender, and this one in Nanobanana.  

Since I’m a beginner, it’s very hard for me to get detailed rendering quickly in Blender.  
Rendering a single image takes a long time, many hours.  
So I use Nanobanana for quick results.  
I just give it a prompt:  
I want a real human face,  
maintain the same makeup,  
keep everything else the same,  
but the face texture must look very real.  
Then it generates this.  
It fits very well with the character I envision.  

On the left, I put this picture into Tab Now.  
It acts like a node in Tab Now, generating a script for my video.  
I know how to edit videos,  
understand the logic and connection between each picture.  

Finally, I use Kling to generate the video.  
Tab Now is a bit expensive.  
I used up my gold coins during the previous period.  
Because I needed to make a long video, at least three to five minutes.  
So I used Kling, which is cheaper and produces good results.  

You can see there are many drafts.  
You have to consider many pre- and post-connections,  
how to shoot the scene,  
the relationship between the character and the scene,  
whether the character is centered or off-center,  
camera angles — up or down,  
origin of the perspective,  
whether it’s a moving or fixed camera.  
All these are essential for visual accumulation.  
This is a comprehensive skill, like a director’s perspective.  

Look at this picture — it’s like a director’s viewpoint.  

So I think this class has brought me a lot.  
These are some screenshots, scenes, clothing shots, some empty screenshots,  
and the far right shows all the makeup,  
which is very difficult to achieve in reality.  

I also did a lot of hyper-realistic work,  
whether in clothing, character style, or scene design.  

Finally, I want to say:  
because I used to be a fashion designer,  
the reason I chose fashion is because I really love handcrafted things.  
I think handcrafted things are livelier and more vital.  

But later, starting from computers and learning techniques,  
I have become very passionate about learning these skills.  
I have experienced psychological struggles,  
but I found that once you take the step to learn,  
you get very good results.  
You can try many things you never dared to think of before.  

What I want to say is, regarding learning techniques,  
for example, AI is very popular now.  
I think originality is very important.  
You must have original ideas to create something good.  
Otherwise, it’s easy to be swept up by big trends,  
making it hard to form your own style.  

Besides AI, learning the techniques themselves is very important,  
whether it’s basic clothing sewing or electronic Clo3D virtual sewing.  
These are all important because knowing the technique helps you realize your ideas better.  

While learning techniques, it is also very important to maintain your subjectivity.  
This way, you won’t be drowned in the AI age.  

Okay, this is my sharing.  
Thank you, everyone.

chunks.content: # CLO 2026 Academic Month **Weaving dreams from scratch, garment assembly by sequence, CLO lets creativity grow freely** --- ## Introduction and Personal Background This section introduces Huang Maihang, a senior fashion designer and student at the Chinese Academy of Fine Arts, outlining her interests and early design style, which integrates vivid, contrasting colors and draws inspiration from makeup and photography. Huang Maihang graduated from Guangzhou Academy of Fine Arts and is currently deepening her fashion design expertise. Alongside fashion, she pursues photography and makeup, which both inspire her design work. Her preferred palette favors vivid, bright colors such as silver and light tones, often using contrasting combinations to express conflict, while rarely relying on black or white except for specific details like teeth. Her early design works strongly influence her 3D creations, blending traditional fashion with digital innovation. These works reflect a consistent style that merges bold colors and complex contrasts, setting the foundation for her academic projects and digital fashion experiments. --- ## Academic Course Structure and Tools Overview This section details the seven-week course framework combining individual and group projects, highlighting the use of Clo3D alongside AI-generated content and multiple 3D software tools. The course spans approximately seven weeks (49 days), divided between individual and group assignments. Individual projects focus on discovering personal design styles and mastering foundational skills quickly. Group projects emphasize collaboration and interpersonal skills. The curriculum encompasses a broad range of digital tools beyond Clo3D, including AI-generated content (AIGC), Nomad, Blender, and TouchDesigner. This multi-application workflow facilitates diverse capabilities, from garment simulation to video production and rendering. Huang emphasizes the transformation of her traditional photography and makeup practices into virtual forms, marking a significant innovation in her creative process. This integration of virtual and traditional techniques is a major step forward in her fashion design journey. --- ## Project Inspiration and Thematic Sources This section explores the emotional and cultural inspirations behind Huang’s project, emphasizing themes of pain, loneliness, and visual styles influenced by cultural references like Pe, Acid Wave, and Eye Spy. The project's core theme revolves around the experience of pain and loneliness, transformed through the use of bright, contrasting colors to avoid overt sadness. The color palette includes reds, greens, yellows, and purples, aiming to evoke numbness or slight discomfort rather than direct pain. Huang draws inspiration from three cultural styles: - **Pe**: An Asian cultural style, often associated with Latino communities, that symbolically expresses identity through teeth imagery. - **Acid Wave**: A visually chaotic music and art style characterized by bright, bumpy, and sour-colored elements. - **Eye Spy**: An intricate visual discovery style composed of delicate scenes with hidden details and accompanying poems, fostering exploration and subtlety. Her designs personify teeth characters, each with distinct personalities correlating to their real-life dental functions: - **Tiger Tooth (Full Tooth)**: Sharp, pointed, dominant teeth symbolized by avant-garde, pungent designs. - **Door Tooth**: The frontmost visible tooth, represented with a formal suit and top hat to emphasize visibility and presence.

chunks.content: - **Acid Wave**: A visually chaotic music and art style characterized by bright, bumpy, and sour-colored elements. - **Eye Spy**: An intricate visual discovery style composed of delicate scenes with hidden details and accompanying poems, fostering exploration and subtlety. Her designs personify teeth characters, each with distinct personalities correlating to their real-life dental functions: - **Tiger Tooth (Full Tooth)**: Sharp, pointed, dominant teeth symbolized by avant-garde, pungent designs. - **Door Tooth**: The frontmost visible tooth, represented with a formal suit and top hat to emphasize visibility and presence. - **Old Tooth**: Large biting teeth, inspiring clothing with bite marks to simulate wear and function. - **Sting Tooth**: The youngest, second-emerging tooth, portrayed as a smart, lively child, adding a unique character dimension. This anthropomorphization ties dental traits to human-like personalities, enriching the conceptual narrative. --- ## Technology Application and Implementation with Clo3D and 3D Tools This section covers the practical use of Clo3D and related 3D software in fashion design, including pattern making, material simulation, workflow integration, and challenges encountered. Clo3D is praised for its efficiency and flexibility, allowing rapid prototyping and experimentation without fear of failure. It significantly reduces the learning curve for pattern making and material simulation, enabling designers to try complex fabric combinations and dynamic effects. Examples include: - Importing 3D assets (e.g., tiger teeth models) into Blender for recoloring while retaining Clo3D’s garment structure. - Simulating cloth properties like shine and texture that are difficult to replicate with traditional fabric. - Attempting craft techniques virtually that are challenging or impossible in real life. Challenges highlighted: - Transitioning from physical to virtual materials involves understanding which real-life actions correspond to software functions. - Issues such as fabric piercing, tearing, and improper inflation require balancing simulation parameters (e.g., internal pressure vs. external pressure). - Gravity and fabric physical properties must be carefully selected to suit the garment’s behavior. - Sewing in Clo3D mimics real-life sewing concepts but often leads to errors due to unfamiliarity with 3D technical operations. Huang emphasizes that mastering these tools is vital as industries like gaming increasingly demand 3D clothing design skills. --- ## Multi-Software Workflow and File Format Management This section explains the multi-step workflow incorporating Clo3D, Nomad, Blender, and AI tools, focusing on compatibility, file formats, and teamwork dynamics. The typical workflow involves: 1. **Clothing design and pattern building in Clo3D.** 2. **Model and accessory adjustments in Nomad**, which offers intuitive sculpting similar to clay modeling and supports pre-rendering. 3. **Rendering and scene finalization in Blender**, where detailed face and makeup adjustments are made. 4. **AI-assisted video generation**, using tools like Nanobanana for face creation and Tab Now and Kling for video scripting and production. File formats encountered include GLTF, MTL, FBX, and proprietary pattern files. Maintaining awareness of software compatibility and proper data transfer is essential to avoid data loss or material deformation. Huang recounts instances where improper file handling caused material damage, necessitating time-consuming rework in Clo3D.

chunks.content: **Rendering and scene finalization in Blender**, where detailed face and makeup adjustments are made. 4. **AI-assisted video generation**, using tools like Nanobanana for face creation and Tab Now and Kling for video scripting and production. File formats encountered include GLTF, MTL, FBX, and proprietary pattern files. Maintaining awareness of software compatibility and proper data transfer is essential to avoid data loss or material deformation. Huang recounts instances where improper file handling caused material damage, necessitating time-consuming rework in Clo3D. Teamwork is facilitated by dividing roles among clothing and makeup design, video production, and scene creation, optimizing the use of each software’s strengths. --- ## AI Integration in Fashion Design and Video Production This section discusses the use of AI tools for rendering, face generation, and video scripting, highlighting the importance of training, creativity, and design knowledge. AI tools like **Nanobanana** and **MidJourney** are employed for rapid rendering and face generation. Nanobanana is favored for its responsiveness to user instructions, while MidJourney often adds unintended elements. AI requires extensive training with detailed prompts to achieve about 70% accuracy, demanding designers have aesthetic sensibilities and design thinking to guide outputs effectively. For video production, **Tab Now** is used to generate scripts and manage visual logic, while **Kling** provides cost-effective video rendering with good results. The video production process involves careful consideration of scene composition, character positioning, camera angles, and movement, akin to a director’s approach to visual storytelling. --- ## Reflections on Learning, Creativity, and Maintaining Originality This final section reflects on Huang’s journey transitioning from traditional fashion design to digital and AI-enhanced workflows, emphasizing the importance of technical mastery, originality, and personal style. Starting from a passion for handcrafted fashion, Huang embraced computer-based techniques, overcoming psychological challenges to achieve new creative possibilities. She stresses the significance of originality amid AI trends, cautioning against losing personal style by merely following popular movements. Learning core skills—such as traditional sewing and virtual garment construction in Clo3D—is crucial for realizing creative ideas effectively. Maintaining subjectivity and independent thinking ensures designers remain distinctive and relevant in an AI-driven era. --- # Summary This document captures Huang Maihang’s comprehensive experience and methodology in integrating traditional fashion design with advanced digital tools like Clo3D, Nomad, Blender, and AI applications. It outlines her academic workflows, creative inspirations, technical challenges, multi-software integration, and reflections on sustaining originality in a rapidly evolving creative landscape.
